title: Uses and applications of electromagnetic waves

notes.definition: Each part of the electromagnetic spectrum has practical uses: radio waves for television and radio, microwaves for satellite communications and cooking, infrared for heaters, cooking and cameras, visible light for fibre optics, ultraviolet for energy efficient lamps and sun tanning, and X-rays and gamma rays for medical imaging and treatments.
explanation: Radio waves are used for television and radio broadcasting. They have the longest wavelengths in the EM spectrum. They can travel long distances through the atmosphere and can pass through walls, so a radio or television indoors can still receive a signal. A transmitter aerial produces them and a receiving aerial absorbs them, so the signal can be picked up.

Microwaves are used for satellite communications and cooking food. The microwaves used for satellites (such as satellite TV and phones) pass through the Earth's atmosphere without being absorbed or reflected much, so they can reach satellites in orbit and return. In a microwave oven, a different wavelength of microwave is absorbed by water molecules in the food. This transfers energy to the food, heating it from within.

Infrared is used in electrical heaters, for cooking food (grills, toasters) and in infrared cameras. Infrared is absorbed by the surfaces of objects and transfers energy to their thermal energy store, warming them. All objects emit infrared, and hotter objects emit more, so an infrared camera can make an image showing temperature differences: useful for finding heat loss from houses, people in the dark or overheating machinery. Visible light is used in fibre optic communications: pulses of light travel along thin glass fibres, reflecting off the inside walls, carrying large amounts of information over long distances with little loss.

Ultraviolet is used in energy efficient lamps and in sun tanning. In an energy efficient lamp, UV is produced inside the tube and absorbed by a coating that then emits visible light. In tanning, UV is absorbed by the skin, which produces a darker pigment. X-rays and gamma rays are used in medical imaging and treatments. X-rays pass easily through soft tissue but are absorbed by dense bone, so they make shadow images of bones. Gamma rays can pass out of the body, so gamma-emitting tracers can be used to image organs; high doses of both can be focused to kill cancer cells in radiotherapy.

Higher tier students must explain why each type of EM wave is suitable for its use. The explanation always links a property of the wave (how far it travels, whether it is absorbed or transmitted by particular materials, how much energy it carries, whether it is ionising) to the job it does. For example, X-rays are suitable for imaging bones because they are transmitted by soft tissue but absorbed by bone; gamma rays are suitable for treating cancer because they are highly penetrating and ionising, so they can reach and kill cells deep inside the body.
keyFacts: Infrared: electrical heaters, cooking food, infrared cameras.
Ultraviolet: energy efficient lamps, sun tanning.
X-rays and gamma rays: medical imaging and treatments.
Satellite microwaves pass through the atmosphere; oven microwaves are absorbed by water in food.
X-rays are absorbed by bone but transmitted by soft tissue.
Higher: the suitability of each wave depends on its properties (absorption, transmission, energy, ionising ability).

keyTerms.definition: A thin, flexible glass fibre that carries pulses of light, used to send information.
Sending signals between the ground and orbiting satellites using microwaves that pass through the atmosphere.
A camera that detects infrared radiation to form an image showing differences in temperature.
Producing pictures of the inside of the body, for example X-ray images of bones.
Treating cancer by using high doses of X-rays or gamma rays to kill cancer cells.
A coating in an energy efficient lamp that absorbs ultraviolet and emits visible light.

workedExamples.title: Matching a wave to a use
workedExamples.question: A security guard needs to see people moving in a dark car park. Which EM wave should the camera detect, and why?
steps: People are warmer than their surroundings.
All objects emit infrared, and hotter objects emit more.
An infrared camera detects this radiation even without visible light.
workedExamples.answer: Infrared, because warm bodies emit more infrared than the cooler surroundings.

workedExamples.title: Higher: explaining suitability
workedExamples.question: Explain why X-rays are suitable for checking whether a bone is broken.
steps: X-rays are transmitted (pass through) soft tissue such as skin and muscle.
X-rays are absorbed by dense materials such as bone.
A detector behind the patient records where X-rays get through; bone leaves a shadow and a break shows as a dark line through it.
workedExamples.answer: X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by bone, so bones show up as shadows and breaks can be seen.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think microwave ovens cook food from the outside in, like an oven.
misconceptions.right: In fact microwaves penetrate a few centimetres into food and are absorbed by water molecules there, heating the food internally.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think radio broadcasts are sent as sound waves.
misconceptions.right: In fact the information is carried by radio waves (EM waves) and converted into sound by the receiver.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think infrared cameras need light to work.
misconceptions.right: In fact they detect infrared emitted by the objects themselves, so they work in complete darkness.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think X-rays show bones because bones glow.
misconceptions.right: In fact bones absorb X-rays, leaving a shadow on the detector, while soft tissue lets X-rays through.

realWorld: Satellite television dishes receive microwaves from satellites 36 000 km above the Earth.
Broadband internet uses optical fibres to carry huge amounts of data as pulses of light.
Firefighters use infrared cameras to find people trapped in smoke-filled buildings.
Gamma rays are used to sterilise surgical instruments and kill bacteria on food.
higherTier: Explain why each type of electromagnetic wave is suitable for the practical application, for example: radio waves travel long distances and pass through walls; satellite microwaves pass through the atmosphere; oven microwaves are absorbed by water in food; infrared is emitted more by hotter objects and absorbed by surfaces; visible light travels along glass fibres; UV is absorbed by fluorescent coatings; X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by bone; gamma rays are penetrating and ionising so can kill cancer cells.
examTips: Learn the specification's list of uses exactly: these are the examples examiners expect.
Higher: when asked why a wave is suitable, give a property AND link it to the use (for example 'absorbed by bone, so bones show up').
Do not confuse the two microwave uses: satellite microwaves pass through the atmosphere; oven microwaves are absorbed by water.
Remember X-rays and gamma rays are used for both imaging and treatment.
If a question asks about risks as well as uses, mention that UV, X-rays and gamma rays are hazardous.
summary: UV: energy efficient lamps, sun tanning.
X-rays and gamma: medical imaging and treatments.
Higher: explain suitability using properties of the waves.

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used for fibre optic communications?
markScheme: 1 mark: Visible light
questions.explanation: The AQA spec lists visible light for fibre optic communications.

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used to cook food in an oven?
markScheme: 1 mark: Microwaves
questions.explanation: Microwave ovens use microwaves that are absorbed by water in food.

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used in electrical heaters?
markScheme: 1 mark: Infrared
questions.explanation: Electrical heaters emit infrared, which is absorbed by objects and warms them.

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used in sun tanning beds?
markScheme: 1 mark: Ultraviolet
questions.explanation: Sun tanning uses ultraviolet. (UV also increases the risk of skin cancer.)

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used to broadcast television and radio?
markScheme: 1 mark: Radio waves
questions.explanation: Radio waves are used for TV and radio broadcasting.

questions.question: Which pair of electromagnetic waves are both used for medical imaging and treatments?
markScheme: 1 mark: X-rays and gamma rays
questions.explanation: X-rays and gamma rays are used for imaging (such as X-ray images and gamma tracers) and treatment (radiotherapy).

questions.question:
An engineer wants to find where energy is being lost from a house at night.
Which device should the engineer use?
markScheme: 1 mark: An infrared camera
questions.explanation: Warmer areas emit more infrared, so an infrared camera shows where the house is losing energy.

questions.question:
A dentist takes an image of a patient's teeth.
Name the type of electromagnetic wave used.
markScheme: 1 mark: X-rays
questions.explanation: Dental images use X-rays, which are absorbed by teeth and bone.

questions.question:
Infrared radiation and microwaves are both used to cook food.
Suggest one difference in how they heat the food.
markScheme: 1 mark: infrared is absorbed at the surface of the food, which then heats the inside by conduction
1 mark: microwaves penetrate further and are absorbed by water molecules inside the food
questions.explanation: This is why grills brown the outside of food while microwave ovens do not.

questions.question:
Electromagnetic waves have many practical uses.
Name four different types of electromagnetic wave.
Give one use for each type of wave.
markScheme: Indicative content (any four correctly matched):
radio waves: television and radio
microwaves: satellite communications, cooking food
infrared: electrical heaters, cooking food, infrared cameras
visible light: fibre optic communications
ultraviolet: energy efficient lamps, sun tanning
X-rays: medical imaging and treatments
gamma rays: medical imaging and treatments
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): four different waves correctly matched to uses.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two correctly matched.
questions.explanation: Use the examples listed in the specification.

questions.question:
X-rays, gamma rays, microwaves and infrared radiation are all used in hospitals or homes.
Choose three of these types of wave.
Explain why each type of wave is suitable for one particular use.
markScheme: Indicative content:
X-rays: imaging bones; transmitted by soft tissue, absorbed by bone so bones show as shadows
gamma rays: treating cancer (radiotherapy) or imaging using tracers; highly penetrating, ionising, kills cancer cells / passes out of the body to be detected
microwaves: cooking; absorbed by water in food, heating it; or satellite communication: pass through atmosphere
infrared: heaters / cooking; absorbed by surfaces, increases thermal energy; or cameras: hotter objects emit more infrared
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): three uses, each with a correct property clearly linked to why it suits the use.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): three uses with some properties, or two well explained.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): uses named with little or no explanation.
questions.explanation: Each explanation should link a property (absorption, transmission, penetration, ionisation) to the job.

questions.question: Which use of electromagnetic waves depends on the waves being absorbed by water molecules?
options: Cooking food in a microwave oven
markScheme: 1 mark: Cooking food in a microwave oven
questions.explanation: Oven microwaves are absorbed by water in food. Satellite microwaves are chosen because they are NOT absorbed much by the atmosphere.

questions.question:
A hospital needs to sterilise surgical instruments sealed in plastic bags.
Which type of electromagnetic wave is most suitable?
markScheme: 1 mark: Gamma rays
questions.explanation: Gamma rays penetrate the packaging and kill bacteria. The other waves would not pass through and kill microorganisms effectively.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows two uses of microwaves.
Which statement about the two uses is correct?

rows: From the ground, through the atmosphere, to a satellite in space
Into the food in a microwave oven

options: Both uses depend on microwaves being absorbed by water
Satellite microwaves are absorbed by the atmosphere and re-emitted
Satellite microwaves pass through the atmosphere, while oven microwaves are absorbed by water in food
Oven microwaves are ionising, which cooks the food
markScheme: 1 mark: Satellite microwaves pass through the atmosphere, while oven microwaves are absorbed by water in food
questions.explanation: Different wavelengths of microwave behave differently: one is transmitted by the atmosphere, the other is absorbed by water. Microwaves are not ionising.

questions.question:
A camera can show images of warm objects in the dark.
Name the type of electromagnetic wave detected by the camera.
markScheme: 1 mark: infrared
questions.explanation: Infrared cameras detect infrared emitted by warm objects.

questions.question:
X-rays and gamma rays are used in hospitals.
Give one use in imaging and one use in treatment.
markScheme: 1 mark: imaging, e.g. X-ray images of bones / gamma tracers to image organs
1 mark: treatment, e.g. radiotherapy to kill cancer cells
questions.explanation: The spec groups both as used for medical imaging and treatments.

questions.question:
A student makes this statement.
'Infrared is used in cameras, heaters and for cooking because it is emitted and absorbed by objects.'
Explain how this property makes infrared suitable for each of these three uses.
markScheme: Indicative content:
all objects emit infrared; hotter objects emit more in a given time
cameras: detect differences in infrared emitted, so warmer objects stand out, even in the dark
heaters: hot element emits lots of infrared which is absorbed by people and objects, warming them
cooking: infrared from a grill or toaster is absorbed by the surface of food, increasing its thermal energy
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): all three uses explained using emission and/or absorption.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two uses with a simple link to infrared.
questions.explanation: Cameras use emission; heaters and cooking use emission by the hot source and absorption by the object.
